chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you catch the Imam having already bowed, and you say the Takbir and bow before he raises his head, then you have caught the Ruk'ah. But if the Imam raises his head before you bow, then the Ruk'ah has been missed by you.

key_terms.إِدْرَاك: To catch or attain (a part of the prayer)
key_terms.فَاتَتْكَ: It has been missed by you

ai.seo_question: How do I know if I have successfully joined the Imam's bowing in congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the precise temporal criterion for catching a Rak'ah in congregational prayer, emphasizing the follower's synchronization with the Imam's physical movements rather than mere presence. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the importance of 'Wujub al-Ta'abbudi' (obligatory following) and clarifies that the validity of the unit depends on the follower completing the bowing action while the Imam is still in it. This specific condition ensures the unity of the prayer structure, a key principle in Shia congregational practice.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When you realise that the Imam has performed Rukū, so you should exclaim a Takbīr and Rukū before he raises his head, so you would have achieved the Rak’at. But if the Imams raises his head before you perform Rukū, you have missed out on the Rak’at’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If you join the Imam for one Rak‘at, say Takbir (Allah is great beyond description). You must perform Ruku‘ (bowing down on one’s knees) before he raises his head (from Ruku‘). You have joined for one Rak‘at but if he raises his head before you are in Ruku‘, you have missed one Rak‘at.’”
